title: PINN optimisation of a planar bifurcation: all results

p: This document gathers every result produced for the paper since the Reynolds-number study began. Part A is the Reynolds-number study of the corner-mode parametric PINN at q = 0.5; Part B answers the paper's outstanding items; Part C collects the finite-element results for layouts other than 30/90 and 30/120; Part D is Tier A, the pre-registered runs at other shares. Accuracy is always measured against the finite-element reference solution, never by loss value.

bullets: Part A. At q = 0.5 the parametric PINN locates 30/90's optimum to within the ±0.002 search tolerance on average at Re_h = 10 (+0.0009 ± 0.0005), with a regret below 0.06% at every Reynolds number; 30/120's minimum lies at the geometry's limit at Re_h ≤ 10, so it tests the pressure drop only.

Part B. Network 1's outlet profile matches the Poiseuille profile u = 1 − y² to 2.7 × 10⁻⁶ (relative L2, mean of three seeds); Table 3's low-Re rows, the solver (SuperLU), Network 1's L-BFGS cycles (4 × 500) and the references are settled.

Part C. Thirteen other layouts have finite-element optima at Re_h = 10 and closed-length maps at six Reynolds numbers; no PINN was trained on them. On six held-out layouts the free length-corrected split s_L has a mean regret of 0.015% against Network 3's 0.016% (worst 0.087% against 0.077%), and the Murray split 0.109%.

Part D. Of 12 pre-registered runs, 2 pass P1 (the PINN's optimum within ±0.002), both at q = 0.5; every off-centre share fails, the symmetric null test included, and at Re_h = 0.1 badly. The share is confounded with a smaller corner-mode cutoff.

note: Part A, 30/90 at q = 0.5: the PINN's optimum minus the reference optimum, over the seeds run at each Reynolds number.

h1: Part A. The Reynolds-number study (30/90 and 30/120, q = 0.5)

p: PINN runs on two bifurcation layouts at several Reynolds numbers, each checked against a finite-element answer key, and the closed-length design maps that show the approach to Murray's law. Every number below is read from the stored result files in docs/re_study and docs/bifurcation_closed-*; the file each table comes from is named under it.

h2: 1. What was run

p: Layouts 30/90 and 30/120 on the existing parametric geometry: parent 3 long, daughters' outer walls 4 long, flow share q = 0.5, split s = w₁/w₀ ∈ [0.35, 0.65]. Corner-mode PINN with the existing schedule (Adam 3,000 steps, L-BFGS 4 × 500, Levenberg–Marquardt 150). Re_h ≤ 1 uses the viscous pressure scale μU_c/h, so the momentum equation reads Re(u·∇)u + ∇p − ∇²u = 0; Re_h ≥ 10 uses ρU_c². At Re_h = 100 the reference is reached by Reynolds continuation through 25 and 50.

p: Definitions. Argmin error = PINN s* − reference s*. Regret = J_ref(s*_PINN)/J_ref* − 1, both values from the reference solution. Drop error = J_PINN/J_ref − 1 at the same split. Field errors are relative L2 errors integrated on the reference mesh. Converged = the schedule finished, every loss finite, and the best held-out loss of the last 25 LM steps not more than 10% below the best before them. Loss is a diagnostic only, never an accuracy measure.

h2: 2. Finite-element answer keys

p: Procedure for each case: a 17-point scan over every split the width bounds allow, Brent to ±0.001 on the search mesh (max area 0.02, 3 corner levels), then the optimum and its grid neighbours on the check mesh (0.005, 5 levels). The argmin bound ε_s is the shift the check mesh's error slope implies plus 0.001. J on the reference mesh (0.002, 6 levels) is measured by the same function that measures the PINNs.

note: Source: docs/re_study/answer_keys.json. J in μU_c/h at Re_h ≤ 1, ρU_c² above.

p: For 30/120 every split below s = 0.268 is refused by the geometry (the inner walls would meet beyond daughter 1's outlet), and J falls toward that limit at every Re_h: the global s_FE = 0.2680 is the geometric limit, not a flow optimum, and has no argmin bound. Inside the PINNs' range the optimum is:

note: At Re_h 0.1, 1 and 10 J rises across the whole range, so the in-range optimum is its lower bound. Only at Re_h = 100 is there an interior optimum; the reference mesh's Brent search puts it at 0.3859 (J is flat there: 0.2% between s = 0.35 and 0.40).
J on the reference mesh at the evaluation splits (for regret and the H3 error slope). Per-case CSVs: docs/re_study/fe_<case>_reference.csv.

h2: 3. Closed-length maps: the approach to Murray's law

p: Both daughters have both walls over 8, so the fully developed friction law puts the optimum exactly at the Murray split s_M and s* − s_M is the junction and entrance effect. Fifteen layouts × eleven shares at each Re_h. Location bound: the mesh-induced argmin shift plus the search tolerance; 'resolved' = beyond its own bound.

Sparse direct solver: SuperLU, through SciPy's spsolve, which scikit-fem's solve calls (UMFPACK is not installed).

h2: 6. Notes

p: The Re_h = 100 run of seed 21 had the lowest held-out loss of the 30/90 runs and the largest argmin error; the only run that met the convergence definition (30/90, Re_h 100, seed 23) has the largest velocity error of the 30/90 runs. Every other run was still improving when the fixed schedule ended.

For 30/120 J rises across [0.35, 0.65] at Re_h 0.1, 1 and 10, and below the range it falls until the geometry refuses the split at s = 0.268. Runs 6 and 7 therefore end on the range's bound with the reference, and test drop and field accuracy only. Run 5 (Re_h 0.1) was stopped at LM step ~100 for that reason and recorded as skipped. Run 8 (Re_h 100) has an interior optimum and is the one 30/120 test of the argmin: the PINN put it at 0.3998 against 0.3859, regret 0.080%.

h1: Part B. The paper's outstanding items

p: This document collects the results requested for the paper: Table 3's rows at Re_h = 0.1 and 1, Network 1's outlet profile against the Poiseuille parabola, two details of the code, three references, and the pressure-drop-error and training figures redrawn with all 13 runs. It also records what the finite-element answer key shows about the 30/120 layout. Every number is read from the stored result files named under each item.

h2: 1. Table 3: the equal-length maps at every Reynolds number

p: Source: docs/re_study/closed-junction-all.json (bifurcation/junction_re.py). In these maps both daughters have both walls over a length of 8, so the friction law's optimum is exactly the Murray split s_M and s* − s_M measures the junction and entrance effect alone. Murray regret = J(s_M)/J* − 1. Optima next to a split with no steady solution are left out.

The text's 'about 0.008' is 0.0080 at Re_h = 0.1 and 0.0080 at Re_h = 1, both at 30/120 with q = 0.9. Its 'about 0.003' (up to 90°) is 0.0033 at Re_h = 0.1 (10/80, q = 0.9) and 0.0031 at Re_h = 1 (0/60, q = 0.8). At both low Reynolds numbers the largest Murray regret, 0.206%, is at the 180° layout 30/150 with q = 0.2. Layout by layout, the largest departures at Re_h = 0.1 and 1 differ by at most 0.0005.

h2: 2. Network 1's outlet profile against the Poiseuille parabola

p: No trained Network 1 had been kept, so it was retrained from its stored configs: G5 (Adam, four L-BFGS cycles, 800 Levenberg–Marquardt steps; developing_flow/re10_lm_fresh_inputmap.yaml) and then its three 100-step, 16,384-point polishes, seeds 1–3 (P7; developing_flow/re10_polish_g5_points*.yaml), which are the three seeds of Table 6.1. The finite-element reference was rebuilt as well and matches the stored one to every printed digit (total-pressure drop 2.1348435579, entrance length 1.7794154129).

h3: Does the retrained network reproduce the stored one?

note: Errors against the finite-element reference, integrated on its mesh (developing_flow/summary_reference.py). Stored: docs/developing_re10-summary.json; retrained: docs/re_study/network1_retrain/summary.json.

p: The retrained networks reproduce the stored errors to every printed digit, so the outlet values below belong to the networks reported in Table 6.1.

The analytical profile is u = 1.5 U (1 − y²) with the mean velocity U = Q₀/2 = 2/3, that is u = 1 − y², v = 0. Each norm is taken across the channel at x = 10 on the reference's 1001 heights (developing_flow/outlet_error.py; docs/developing_re10-outlet.md).

p: Network 1's outlet profile agrees with the analytical Poiseuille profile to a relative L2 error of 2.7 × 10⁻⁶ (mean of three seeds; 1.4 × 10⁻⁶ to 3.8 × 10⁻⁶). The reference itself departs from it by 4.5 × 10⁻⁸ there, so the network's error is its own, not the reference's. h2: 3. Two details from the code

bullets: Sparse direct solver (Section 3.2): SuperLU. Each Newton step's linear system is solved by scikit-fem's solve, which calls SciPy's spsolve; UMFPACK (scikits.umfpack) is not installed, so spsolve uses SuperLU (checked on this machine: SciPy 1.17.1, scikit-fem 12.0.2). Its reference is Li, X. S. (2005). An overview of SuperLU: Algorithms, implementation, and user interface. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 31(3), 302–325. https://doi.org/10.1145/1089014.1089017 (DOI confirmed against the ACM Digital Library's listing).
L-BFGS iterations per cycle (Section 3.3): 500, in 4 cycles (gtol 1e-14), from developing_flow/re10_lm_fresh_inputmap.yaml. Network 1's final 100-step polish uses no L-BFGS.

h2: 6. 30/120: its 'optimum' is the edge of the feasible splits

p: The finite-element answer key gave s_FE = 0.2680 for 30/120 at every Reynolds number. That value is not a minimum of J. Below s = 0.26753 the geometry is refused, because the inner walls meet beyond an outlet, and J is still falling at the last split that can be built. There, daughter 1's walled length is 0.0006: the 30° branch has all but vanished. The answer key now marks the value as a geometry limit (docs/re_study/answer_keys.md).

note: Search-mesh J (μU_c/h at Re_h ≤ 1, ρU_c² above). Splits below 0.26753 are refused.

bullets: Retraining on a range around 'its real optimum' is therefore not possible: [0.15, 0.45] cannot be built, and a range starting at 0.27 would put the answer on its own lower edge again, which tests nothing. It was not run.

At Re_h ≤ 10 the 30/120 runs test pressure-drop and field accuracy only. At Re_h = 100 the range holds a genuine local minimum (0.3797 on the search mesh, 0.3859 on the reference mesh), which the PINN located to 0.014 (regret 0.08%), but J at the limit is lower still (0.3984 against 0.4247 on the search mesh).

The 165 optima behind Table 3 were checked for the same failure and none has it. The only optimum at a geometry limit in those maps is the equal-outlet-pressure row for 30/150 (s = 0.8987 against a closed entrance at 0.8992), which is not one of the 165.

p: s_L solves s/(1 − s) = (L₁/L₂)^(1/4) √(q/(1 − q)) with L₁ and L₂ measured on the geometry at s_L itself (q = 0.5; parent 3, outer walls 4, as in the answer key).

note: The answer key's 2.0003 and 6.4638 are the centreline lengths at the 0.2680 limit, not at s_L. For comparison, 30/90 gives s_L = 0.4843 (L₁ = 3.6841, L₂ = 4.7386).

h1: Part C. The other layouts (finite elements and Network 3)

p: The PINNs (Networks 1 and 2, and the parametric Network 2) were trained only on 30/90 and 30/120, so every result below for other layouts is finite-element data, plus Network 3's predictions on its held-out layouts. A layout a1/a2 names the two daughters' angles from the parent's axis; s = w1/w0 is the width split and q daughter 1's share of the flow. J is the total-pressure drop in ρU_c². s_M is the planar Murray split, √q/(√q + √(1 − q)): a channel's resistance goes as 1/w³, so the widths go as the square root of the flow, not the cube root of a pipe.

h2: 3. Six held-out layouts: Network 3 against the simple rules

p: Network 3 was trained on the 165 optima of Section 1 and tested on six layouts it never saw, each at three shares, every case optimised separately by finite elements (Re_h = 10, daughters 8 long). Regret = J(s)/J* − 1 for adopting split s instead of s*.

h2: 4. What there is no data for

bullets: No PINN of any kind was trained on a layout other than 30/90 and 30/120, so there are no PINN field errors, pressure-drop errors or PINN optima for the other 13 layouts.

Flow-field pictures exist for the 15 layouts at their Re_h = 10 optima at q = 0.5 and 0.2 (docs/fields/gallery_q*.png).

h1: Part D. Tier A: new shares and a symmetric control

p: Twelve parametric PINN runs, one seed each (21), at Re_h = 0.1 and 10: 30/90 at q = 0.2, 0.35, 0.65 and 0.8; 15/15 at q = 0.2 (the null test); 0/120 at q = 0.5. Rules and pass marks were committed before any screening solve or run (docs/re_study/tierA/preregistration.md). P1: the PINN's optimum within ±0.002 of the reference optimum (Brent on the reference mesh). P2: the reference optimum within 0.003 of the length-corrected split s_L, where no daughter turns beyond 90° (30/90 and 15/15). Both tolerances are the paper's, unchanged. Each trained range is s_L ± 0.15; all twelve cases passed the screening for an interior minimum with daughters 4 long (docs/re_study/tierA/screening.md).
Of the 12 runs reported, 2 pass P1. Of the 10 in P2's scope, 5 pass P2. Verdicts are on the unrounded values; nothing was rerun.

h2: What Tier A shows

bullets: P1 passes only at q = 0.5: 0/120 at both Reynolds numbers, to within 0.0001. Every run at another share fails it, at both Reynolds numbers, including the symmetric 15/15 null test.

At Re_h = 10 the misses are moderate and grow with the share's distance from 0.5: −0.0049 at q = 0.35, +0.0020 at 0.65 (failing by 0.00002), −0.0064 at 0.8, −0.0078 at 0.2, and −0.0068 for 15/15 at 0.2. The regret stays below 0.13%, and the pressure-drop error within ±2.6% over each off-centre range (±3.2% for 0/120).

At Re_h = 0.1 every off-centre run fails, by +0.006 to +0.156 (regret up to 40%; the PINN's optimum always lies above the reference's). Every Tier A run there, 0/120 included, ends at a held-out loss of 1.1 to 22, against 0.12 to 0.16 for the three earlier 30/90 runs at q = 0.5, and with largest drop errors of 8 to 30%; 0/120 (1.1, −8.1% at its range's top) still placed its optimum to 0.0001, because its error was flat near the optimum.
The 15/15 null test misses by as much as 30/90 at the same share (−0.0068 against −0.0078 at Re_h = 10), so the miss belongs to the share, not to the layout's length asymmetry.

Confound: every off-centre case also had a smaller corner-mode cutoff (0.10 to 0.35, by the pre-registered rule, because its narrow daughter is narrow) than 0/120 (0.40) or the earlier runs (0.5). Tier A cannot separate the share from the cutoff; a run at an off-centre share with the cutoff held at 0.40 or more would, where the geometry admits it (it does not at q = 0.2 or 0.8 with this range).

P2, a property of the reference solution: s_L lies within 0.003 of the optimum at q = 0.35 and 0.65 at Re_h = 0.1, q = 0.35 at 10, and for 15/15 at both; it does not at q = 0.2 and 0.8 for 30/90 (0.004 to 0.006), nor at q = 0.65 at Re_h = 10 (0.0031). The length correction loses accuracy as the share moves from 0.5 in a layout with unequal lengths.
